extraction_notes.note: Symbols are introduced in 'where ...' clauses that continue the sentence containing a numbered display; whole-sentence boundaries force these definition nodes to contain the numbered equation, which is nested in them.

The paper's main result (closed-form approximate sum-rate) is an unnamed numbered equation reached by a derivation in running text; kept as equation rather than a claim with a prose proof, and the derivation is recorded as uses edges between the equations.
The three-phase two-way DASTC transmission protocol is described in prose; extracted as an unmarked algorithm with one step per phase.
Figure-only numerical results (sum-rate curves) and the prose derivation text between equations in Section 3 (e.g. det(I+AB)=det(I+BA), 'Similarly ... I_2') were not made separate nodes.

nodes.name: Channel reciprocity
nodes.statement: Due to the channel reciprocity, we note that channel gains of $\mathsf{A} \longrightarrow \mathsf{B}$ and $\mathsf{B} \longrightarrow \mathsf{A}$ links, with $\mathsf{A}, \mathsf{B} \in \{\Source{1},\Source{2},\mathsf{R}\}$, are identical.

nodes.name: Two-way AF distributed Alamouti space-time code (DASTC) scheme
nodes.statement:
The communications of the proposed two-way AF DASTC scheme occur in three phases. In the first phase, both $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ transmit the first row of Alamouti code \cite{Ala:98:JSAC} to $\mathsf{R}$ with the same transmit power per symbol $\mathcal{P}_s$. The received signal at the relay $\mathsf{R}$ is given by  egin{align} \y{R} = \h{1} \s{1} + \h{2} \x{1} + \B{n}_{\mathsf{R}} \end{align} where $\s{1}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{s_1 } & {s_2 } \ \end{array}}]$ and $\x{1}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{x_1 } & {x_2 } \ \end{array}}]$ are the two first rows of the Alamouti codes generated by $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, respectively. The channel coefficients for the link from $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$ to $\mathsf{R}$, respectively denoted as $\h{1}$ and $\h{2}$, follow a Rayleigh distribution, i.e., $\h{1} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{1}}$ and $\h{2} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{2}}$. The vector $\B{n}_{\mathsf{R}}$ is the complex additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) with zero mean and variance $N_0$. In the second phase, $\mathsf{R}$ amplifies the received signal, i.e., $\y{R}$, with the same power constraint as in the first phase and forwards to $\Source{2}$ while $\Source{1}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{2}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{2}$, $\y{2}$, is written as  egin{align} \y{2} = \h{2} G \y{R} + \h{0} \s{2} + 
{2} \end{align} where $G$ is the scalar amplifying gain at the relay, $\h{0} \sim \CG{0}{\CP{0}}$ is the channel gain for the link between $\Source{1}$ and $\Source{2}$, $\s{2}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{-s_2^{\ast} } & {s_1^{\ast} } \ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of the Alamouti code, and $
{2}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$. Similarly, in the third phase, $\mathsf{R}$ transmit $G \y{R}$ whereas $\Source{2}$ sends the second row of the Alamouti code to $\Source{1}$. The received signal at the source $\Source{1}$, $\y{1}$, is shown as  egin{align} \y{1} = \h{1} G \y{R} + \h{0} \x{2} + 
{1} \end{align} where $\x{2}= [ { egin{array}{*{20}c}{-x_2^{\ast} } & {x_1^{\ast} } \ \end{array}}]$ is the second row of Alamouti code and $
{1}$ is the AWGN vector with zero mean and variance $N_0$.

nodes.name: Average sum-rate
nodes.statement: As mentioned above, since the channel model is assumed to be ergodic block fading, we can describe the average sum-rate as follows: \begin{align} C_{\text{sum}} &= \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+G^2 |\h{2}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{s}}\B{h} \right) \nonumber \\ &+ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+ G^2 |\h{1}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{x}}\B{h} \right) \biggr\} \end{align} where $\R{\B{s}}$ and $\R{\B{x}}$ are the covariance matrices of Gaussian codewords and the pre-factor $2/3$ accounts for the fact that each source received information consisting of two symbols over three time slots.
nodes.section: 3 Average Sum-Rate of Distributed Alamouti Space-Time Codes with Two-Way AF Relaying
nodes.statement_short: Average sum-rate as the expectation of 2/3 times the sum of the two log-det mutual informations of the equivalent Alamouti channels.

nodes.statement: C_{\text{sum}} &= \mathbb{E} \biggl\{ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+G^2 |\h{2}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{s}}\B{h} \right) \nonumber \\ &+ \frac{2}{3}\log_2\det\left(\B{I}_2 + \frac{1}{N_0\left(1+ G^2 |\h{1}|^2\right)} \B{h}^{\dag}\R{\B{x}}\B{h} \right) \biggr\}

nodes.name: PDF of the ratio Z = g_i g_j/(g_i+2 g_j)
nodes.statement: Let $\snri{i}$ and $\snri{j}$ be statistically independent and not necessarily identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) exponential random variables with hazard rate $\snravei{i}$ and $\snravei{j}$, respectively. Suppose that the ratio of $Z$ takes the form \begin{align} Z=\frac{\snri{i} \snri{j}}{\snri{i} +2\snri{j}} \end{align} Then, we obtain the PDF of random variable $Z$ as \begin{align} \PDF{Z}{z} = \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \left[\alpha\Bessel{0}{\alpha z} + \beta_i \Bessel{1}{\alpha z}\right] \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$. \begin{proof} Let us rewrite $Z$ in a more tractable form as \begin{align} Z = \left(X + Y\right)^{-1} \end{align} where $X=1/\snri{i}$ and $Y=2/\snri{j}$. Then, after some algebraic simplifications together with the help of \cite[eq.~(3.471.9)]{GR:00:Book}, the moment generating function (MGF) of $X$ and $Y$ can be expressed as, respectively \begin{align} &\MGF{X}{s} = \EXs{X}{\exp\left(-s x\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \\ &\MGF{Y}{s} = \EXs{Y}{\exp\left(-s y\right)} = 2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} As can be seen from \eqref{eq:Z}, since $1/Z$ is the sum of two statistically independent random variables, by using \eqref{eq:MGF:X} and \eqref{eq:MGF:Y}, the MGF of $1/Z$ can be expressed as \begin{align} \MGF{1/Z}{s} = 4\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}s \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{s}{\snravei{i}}}} \Bessel{1}{2 \sqrt{\frac{2s}{\snravei{j}}}} \end{align} Then, the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of $1/Z$, $\CDF{1/Z}{x}$, can be shown as \begin{eqnarray} \CDF{1/Z}{x} =1- \mathcal{L}^{-1}\{\MGF{1/Z}{s}/s\}|_{1/x} \end{eqnarray} where $\mathcal{L}^{-1}\{.\}$ stands for the inverse Laplace transform. From \eqref{eq:MGF:1:Z} and \eqref{eq:CDF:1:Z} together with \cite[eq.~(13.2.20)]{RK:66:Book}, we have \begin{align} \CDF{Z}{z} = 1 - \alpha z \exp\left(-\beta_i z\right) \Bessel{1}{\alpha z} \end{align} where $\alpha = 2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\snravei{i}\snravei{j}}}$ and $\beta_i = \frac{1}{\snravei{j}} + \frac{2}{\snravei{i}}$. By differentiating \eqref{eq:CDF:Z:1} with respect to $z$ and using the fact that $\tfrac{d\Bessel{v}{z}}{dz}=-\Bessel{v-1}{z}-\tfrac{v}{z}\Bessel{v}{z}$ \cite[eq.~(8.486.12)]{GR:00:Book}, we obtain \eqref{eq:PDF:Z:1} which completes the proof. \end{proof}

onumber \ &	imes \left[ 2\Bessel{0}{ rac{2w}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}} + \left( rac{\snravei{1}+\snravei{2}}{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}ight) \Bessel{1}{ rac{2w}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}} ight] \end{align} By substituting \eqref{eq:PDF:W:1} in \eqref{eq:CDF:T:1} and taking the derivative with respect to $t$, we obtain the PDF of $T$ as  egin{align} \PDF{T}{t} = \sum\limits_{n=1}^{2} \varpi_n \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} w^2 &\exp\left[-\left( rac{t}{\snravei{0}}+ rac{1}{\snravei{1}}+ rac{1}{\snravei{2}}ight)wight] 
onumber \ &	imes \Bessel{n}{ rac{2w}{\sqrt{\snravei{1}\snravei{2}}}} dw \end{align} It is observed that the integral given in \eqref{eq:PDF:T:2} can be simplified by using \cite[eq.~(6.621.3)]{Prudnikov:90:Book} which results in \eqref{eq:PDF:T:1}. This completes the proof.
